Subject: Triton Health: post-demo evaluation & quantization tradeoffs

Hi Mike —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and suggested next steps from our demo and discovery: 

- Core ask: Triton wants to extract clinical entities and summarize encounter notes with <1s latency per short note and stable F1 on entities (~95 target).
- Recommended baseline models to evaluate (hosted & private options):
  * Redwood-3B-Response-v2 (FP16) — best balance for latency-sensitive paths.
  * OpenLlama-13B-Refined (AWQ-8) — strong quality for longer context, lower cost after quant.
  * Llama-2-13B-GPTQ (8-bit GPTQ) — higher throughput but watch entity fidelity on some prompts.

Quantization and throughput tuning notes (high-level):
- AWQ (our AWQ pipeline): minimal quality degradation on entity extraction in our internal tests; good latency gains on T4/A10-class GPUs.
- GPTQ: more aggressive size/speed wins but some risk of edge-case hallucinations for clinical abbreviations; requires careful prompt-set evaluation.
- FP8: excellent latency on newer accelerators (A100X/MI300) but limited portability and potential variance across vendor drivers.

Attachments I dropped: triton_postcall_notes.pdf (call notes + action items), throughput-benchmarks.csv (sample latencies/throughput), prompt-set-v1.txt (initial scoring prompts).

Proposed next steps:
1) You confirm a 2-week eval window and scope (we recommend a 1k-note canonical set + 200 annotation checks).
2) We run parallel comparisons: Redwood-3B FP16 vs OpenLlama-13B AWQ vs Llama-2-13B GPTQ; measure entity F1, hallucination rate, median latency, and cost/token.
3) Weekly checkpoints: quick sync day 3 and day 10, final readout and recommendation.

Can you confirm availability for the kickoff on Monday (Apr 19) or Tue (Apr 20)? Also please confirm who will own the annotated sample and whether procurement needs any specific pre-PO paperwork.

Thanks —

Hi Mike —

Looping in a few technical details to address the compliance and rollback questions. Short answers first: yes, we can pin model versions and enable immediate fallback; yes, we can run the eval in us-east-1 only (hosted) if you require — we will isolate logs and apply a 90-day retention policy.

Quantization tradeoffs (more detail):
- AWQ-8 (recommended for OpenLlama-13B here): in our internal entity extraction suites we see mean F1 drop <1.5% vs FP16 on clinical NER, with 2-3x token throughput improvements on T4/A10. Stability is high across prompt variants.
- GPTQ-8: 3-6% variability on rare entity forms (dosage strings, compound drug names). Good cost reduction but requires per-prompt calibration.
- FP8 (hardware dependent): best latency, but you must validate across your infra matrix. FP8 also complicates reproducibility for audit trails unless you lock accelerator/driver stacks.

Evaluation metrics & acceptance criteria (proposal):
- Entity F1 (micro) >= 94.5
- Hallucination rate < 2% on a 200-sample blind set
- Median P95 latency < 1.2s for 1-2 sentence notes
- Regression alerting: if any model variant drops Entity F1 by >1.5 points vs baseline FP16, automatic canary rollback to FP16 and alert to your team

Operational plan:
1) You hand us the 1k canonical notes (we recommend scrambled/hashed PHI in initial pass) + 200 annotated checks.
2) We run parallel endpoints with canary routing in Redwood Dedicated (or Hosted with region pinning) and stream detailed token-level latency + cost breakdown to a shared dashboard.
3) Mid-run check on day 3; final evaluation on day 14 with a short readout.

Attachments: throughput-benchmarks.csv shows our nominal latencies for AWQ vs GPTQ vs FP16 on representative hardware. Prompt-set-v1.txt contains the scoring prompts we used in the demo — please flag any items that require clinical phrasing changes.

If procurement needs a draft SOW I can paste a short outline after we confirm kickoff.

Best,
